responsibilities.label: Maintenance
responsibilities.explanation: Keeping the database software and infrastructure updated. The provider handles routine work, but you may still need to schedule maintenance or plan major engine upgrades.

responsibilities.label: Connection pooling
responsibilities.explanation: Reusing database connections instead of opening a new one for every request. Most services require choosing and configuring a client pool or proxy. D1 uses a Worker binding rather than a traditional connection pool.

responsibilities.label: Concurrent requests
responsibilities.explanation: Handling requests that arrive at the same time. Managed does not mean unlimited: concurrency, connections and throughput have limits. D1 executes queries serially within each database instance.

responsibilities.label: Backups / PITR
responsibilities.explanation: Backups keep recoverable copies. Point-in-time recovery (PITR) lets you recover to a point inside a retained history window. Availability, retention and charges depend on the plan; having backups does not prove a restore will meet your needs.

responsibilities.label: Restore
responsibilities.explanation: Recovering data from a backup or history. You choose the recovery point, start the restore and validate the result. Some services create a new database or cluster, so reconnecting your application can be part of recovery.

responsibilities.label: Compute scaling
responsibilities.explanation: Changing the processing capacity available to the database. Manual includes enabling autoscaling and setting bounds: once configured, it can run automatically. D1 does not expose a database compute-size setting.

responsibilities.label: Storage growth
responsibilities.explanation: Increasing the room available for data. Some services grow storage automatically within limits; others require settings or a plan change. At a per-database cap you may need to split data across databases.

responsibilities.label: Read replicas
responsibilities.explanation: Copies used to serve reads. You may need to create replicas and route reads explicitly. Replication can lag; consistency settings matter. A replica is not an independent historical backup.

responsibilities.label: HA / failover
responsibilities.explanation: High availability (HA) reduces downtime when infrastructure fails. Failover switches to a healthy replacement. Local recovery, zone redundancy and cross-region recovery are different guarantees; verify the service and plan rather than treating Auto as zero downtime.

responsibilities.label: Long-term backups
responsibilities.explanation: Keeping recoverable data beyond the normal backup or PITR window. You choose retention, export destinations and access controls, and test recovery. Export storage and tooling may be separate services.

responsibilities.label: Monitoring / alerts
responsibilities.explanation: Watching database health, usage and failures. Providers expose metrics, but you select alert thresholds, notification destinations and response procedures. Metrics alone do not notify you or fix an incident.
